routes.label: Divide the flag into square cells

question:
Betsy designed a flag using blue triangles, small white squares, and a red center square, as shown. Let \(B\) be the total area of the blue triangles, \(W\) the total area of the white squares, and \(R\) the area of the red square. Which of the following is correct?

[Figure 1](figures/2002_AMC_12A_Q08_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Extend the four sides of the red square to the boundary of the flag. This separates the flag into nine square cells, with the red square as the center cell. Each of the other eight cells contains a white square joining its side midpoints. These midpoint relationships follow from the bisecting diagonals of the white squares and the straight continuations of their sides through the touching vertices.

[Figure 1](figures/2002_AMC_12A_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

Let each cell have side length \(s>0\). In an outer cell, the four triangles outside the white square each have perpendicular legs \(s/2\), so their combined area is
\[
4\left(\frac12\cdot\frac{s}{2}\cdot\frac{s}{2}\right)=\frac{s^2}{2}.
\]
The white square therefore also has area \(s^2-s^2/2=s^2/2\). Thus each of the eight outer cells contains equal blue and white areas. These cells cover every blue and white region without overlapping interiors, so
\[
B=8\cdot\frac{s^2}{2}=W.
\]
The correct choice is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
